A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LeAD-M3D. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across additions, relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original LeAD-M3D experiments on KITTI, Waymo and Rope3D, nuScenes-to-KITTI generalization, and extensive accuracy, ablation and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds component ablations, saliency analyses, teacher-size comparisons and KITTI-to-nuScenes generalization results.

M1.justification: The proposed architecture, A2D2 distillation loss, CM3D matching and CGI3D inference procedure remain unchanged, including Appendix A and Algorithm 1. Newly tested component removals and teacher sizes are experimental controls, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: v3 adds KITTI-to-nuScenes generalization and an in-domain nuScenes evaluation reference in Table 30. v2 evaluated generalization in the opposite direction only. This extends the target-domain test scenario while retaining the same datasets and monocular detection task.

E2.justification: The existing comparisons retain their comparator membership. New Table 30 compares against GUPNet, MonoUNI, MonoLSS, MonoMAE, MonoCon, MonoCD and DEVIANT, a different comparator group from the retained domain-generalization comparison in Table 5. These methods appeared elsewhere in v2 but were not participants in this cross-domain comparison.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce independent denoising/distillation toggles, removal of the matching classification score, CGI3D on/off controls across model sizes, and a smaller-teacher control. Table 30 introduces depth-range mean absolute error under the KITTI-to-nuScenes protocol. Existing training schedules, preprocessing, benchmark protocols and timing procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands analysis of why the components work: Table 16 separates denoising from distillation, Table 18 tests classification confidence in matching, and integrated-gradient examples examine object versus background attention. It also adds CGI3D analysis across all model sizes, teacher-size sensitivity and reverse-direction domain generalization. These answer distinct questions beyond v2's retained ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed variation, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both already describe 1,000 timing passes with median runtime and approximately ±0.2 AP variation from TensorRT quantization. v3 adds no uncertainty-estimation procedure or repeated-run disclosure.

E6.justification: Substantial new findings include Table 16's moderate AP values of 19.12/20.43/20.85/22.65 for neither component, denoising alone, distillation alone and both; and Table 30's 1.07 m cross-domain depth error versus DEVIANT's 1.26 m. Retained results also change: model B's easy/moderate/hard validation AP becomes 28.44/22.65/19.87 instead of 28.33/22.72/19.98. Model N runtime changes from 9.7 to 8.2 ms in updated tables, although other v3 tables still report 9.7 ms. Headline KITTI test, Waymo and Rope3D scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, matching scores and loss formulations in Equations 1–19 are retained. The added mechanism discussion and saliency evidence introduce no new formal assumptions, propositions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same three contributions and accuracy, efficiency and generalization claims. Added experiments support those existing claims. The conclusion is shortened, while the speculative zero-shot research direction remains in Appendix C.

C2.justification: New Section 4.5 interprets denoising as regularization toward object structure and distillation as guidance. Appendix additions explain the matching classification score through foreground/background discrimination and hypothesize memory-bandwidth and synchronization effects behind runtime savings across model sizes. Existing occlusion observations and future-work boundaries remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the architecture details, pseudocode, loss weights, optimizer, training epochs, resolutions, augmentation settings and hardware/TensorRT measurement information. The project URL is unchanged. Added experimental controls do not disclose a revised implementation or new code/data access arrangement.

R1.justification: v3 adds Sundararajan et al.'s integrated-gradients work and a bibliography entry for Zhou et al.'s rotation representations. Existing references and substantive research positioning are retained. Many citation-number changes reflect separating appendix references from the main bibliography.

P1.justification: v3 adds Section 4.5 and focused appendix subsections, revises the appendix roadmap, shortens the conclusion, and makes localized wording, affiliation and acknowledgment edits. References are split between the main paper and supplement. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds four tables (16, 18, 22 and 30) and two saliency figures, with corresponding reflow and renumbering. Existing diagrams, benchmark-table structures and qualitative examples are retained. The new main-text saliency figure and retained appendix MixUp illustration both carry the label Figure 6.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, the separated denoising/distillation controls, matching-score ablation and reverse-domain evaluation strengthen component attribution and generalization evidence. These provide a limited net improvement. However, runtime reporting becomes inconsistent: v3 Tables 9 and 20 give 8.2 ms for model N, while Tables 21 and 22 give 9.7 ms without an explained setting difference, weakening confidence in the precise efficiency measurements.
